cards.text: David wrote this song to God, and the heading tells you when. Saul, Israel's king (1 Samuel 11:15), had sent men to watch David's house so they could kill him. Picture it, friend: you peek through the blinds, and the welcome committee is a hit squad.

cards.question: Saul's men are watching David's house. What's the first thing David asks God for?

answers.text: To deliver him from his enemies
To give him a sword to fight back
To help him make peace with Saul

cards.text: He says it again: save me from men of bloodshed. Then he tells God to look at them lying in wait, and I bet he's not sleeping a wink.

cards.question: Fierce men are plotting against David. David admits he did something to bring this on himself.

cards.text: No fault of his own, and they're rushing to attack him anyway. David doesn't whisper this one: "Arise to help me, and take notice."

cards.question: David calls on the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, to rouse Himself against all the nations. What does David ask for the wicked traitors?

cards.text: Then David paints what's out there: snarling like dogs, prowling around the city. Me? I'd be under the blanket. Under the blanket's BLANKET.

cards.question: Snarling like dogs and prowling around the city, David's enemies return in the ___.

cards.text: And David says, look what spews out of their mouths: sharp words from their lips. That's not a stakeout, friend. That's a group chat with the caps lock stuck.

cards.question: David's enemies are spewing sharp words. What do they say that shows what they're thinking?

answers.text: They think nobody can hear them
They think David will give up
They think the king will reward them

cards.question: David's enemies say nobody can hear them. But David says the LORD ___ at them.

cards.text: He laughs, and He scoffs at all the nations. Snarling dogs, sharp words, a whole stakeout, and the LORD isn't rattled, while me, a drawer opened and I held my breath for a WEEK.
Then David turns his eyes away from the window. He calls God his strength and his fortress.

cards.question: Saul's men are watching David's house. But David says he will keep watch for ___.

cards.text: Then he says it straight: my God of loving devotion will come to meet me. Not might. Not maybe. WILL.

cards.question: David says God will let him stare down his foes.

cards.text: Then David asks God NOT to kill them. Wait. WHAT? Killers at the door, and he says don't kill them?

cards.question: Why does David ask God not to kill his enemies?

answers.text: So his enemies can turn back
So he can face them himself

cards.text: Instead, he asks God to scatter them by His power and bring them down. And he calls Him O Lord, our shield.

cards.question: David's enemies have been spewing sharp words. What does David ask for them to be trapped in?

cards.text: Then he prays for God to consume them in wrath, till they are no more. And he says what he wants people to know: that God rules over Jacob.

cards.question: David wants it known that God rules over Jacob. How far does he want it known?

answers.text: To the ends of the earth

cards.text: That line again: they return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city, scavenging for food and growling when they aren't satisfied. Friend, that's me staring down an oven timer with four minutes left.

cards.question: The dogs come back in the evening. But David says he will proclaim God's loving devotion in the ___.
David sings of God's strength and calls God his refuge in times of trouble.

cards.text: He finishes singing praises with names he's already given God: O my strength, my fortress, my God of loving devotion. Killers at the door and David's SINGING, while I spent years in a drawer and didn't so much as hum.

findings.problem: David shows up for the first time and is never introduced. Saul gets a short introduction, but David doesn't, for example as the young man Saul was hunting or as Israel's future king.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: "Then David paints what's out there…" / "Me?" / "I'd be under the blanket." / "Under the blanket's BLANKET."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "springtime" is a season. "evening" and "daylight" are times of day, so the answers aren't the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the verse line, "That's not a stakeout, friend." and "That's a group chat with the caps lock stuck."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Snarling dogs" drops the text's "like." Psalm 59:6 says the enemies are snarling like dogs, not that they are dogs.

The question sets up Saul's men watching the house, and then offers "Saul's men" as a wrong answer for who David keeps watch for. With men outside waiting to kill him, a baker could argue that David keeps watch for Saul's men.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: "Then he says it straight…" / "Not might." / "Not maybe." / "WILL."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: "Then David asks God NOT to kill them." / "Wait." / "WHAT?" / "Killers at the door, and he says don't kill them?"

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Jacob appears for the first time ("God rules over Jacob") and isn't explained. A baker may read it as Jacob the man, not the people of Israel.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "The dogs come back in the evening" drops the text's "like." Psalm 59:14 says the enemies return snarling like dogs, not that they are dogs.
